title: The NASA Color
slide_intent: Teach designers when a signature color can carry the identity. The ground and surrounding colors influence whether the hue receives attention.
strategic_value: NASA can associate its red with the motion of its letterforms. The manual presents the warm color as an expression of the agency’s forward-looking character.
demonstration: A red logotype stands alone on white. The text specifies a white or light neutral ground and describes when a second color is appropriate.
practical_value: Use this example to decide whether a reproduction has the light ground and color capacity to support NASA red.

content_islands.name: Color guidance
content_islands.spec: Set the title and short guidance in the upper columns. Describe the hue, its intended character and the conditions for using it.

content_islands.name: Red logotype
content_islands.spec: Place one large red master on an uninterrupted white field across the lower portion of the page.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text connects the warm red to kinetic letterforms and NASA’s lively, future-oriented character.
reference_purposes.Expression: A large red logotype on white presents the signature hue without competing elements.
reference_purposes.Application: The guidance places NASA red on white or a light neutral when a second color is available and appropriate.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The text rules out competing bright saturated colors and medium- or dark-value colors that dilute red’s impact.

ingredient.name: NASA red logotype
ingredient.role: Give the letterforms the active, future-oriented character described by the manual.
ingredient.application: Use NASA red when a second color is available and appropriate, on white or a light-value neutral. Avoid the competing saturated and medium-to-dark colors named in the guidance.
ingredient.scope: The 1976 manual’s logotype guidance in section 1.3. Section 1.4 gives specific background cases; this scan is not a calibrated color specification.
